selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does this part say will be discussed in four questions?
questions.answer: Two dangers that make faith feel shaky and bring doubts.

questions.question: What are these questions meant to address?
questions.answer: Two deep causes of doubt in faith today.

questions.question: In the moon example, who gives the strong proof?
questions.answer: The two ordinary men who saw it.

questions.question: If two people truly see the moon, what do they have?
questions.answer: A real witness.

questions.question: When people affirm something with proof, how do they help each other?
questions.answer: They support one another and become stronger together.

questions.question: Why does negation not lead to the same unity?
questions.answer: Because each denial comes from a separate person’s limits.

questions.question: If someone says a thing does not exist anywhere, what very hard job would he need to do?
questions.answer: He would need to search everywhere very fully.

questions.question: What blocks deniers from true judgment?
questions.answer: Their own veils and causes of not seeing.

questions.question: What should he not claim as a fact?
questions.answer: He should not claim that it truly does not exist at all.

questions.question: What does this passage focus on instead of giving the full long explanation?
questions.answer: It gives only two deep dangers that trouble faith in this time.

questions.question: So what does this part choose to explain briefly?
questions.answer: Two dangers that shake certainty.

questions.question: What example is used to show this?
questions.answer: Looking for the new Ramadan moon.

questions.question: If a few people truly see the moon, what kind of evidence is that?
questions.answer: Positive evidence.

questions.question: Why do people who prove something become stronger together?
questions.answer: Because they point to the same real thing.

questions.question: How do people who deny a fact stand?
questions.answer: Each one stands alone.

questions.question: Is it easy to show that something exists?
questions.answer: Yes, one sign can be enough.

questions.question: What do deniers often use to judge?
questions.answer: Their own small view and understanding.

questions.question: Which sentence is careful and honest: “I do not see it” or “It is not real at all”?
questions.answer: “I do not see it.”

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the number of people against belief?
questions.answer: Big numbers do not give real strength to denial.

questions.question: How many deep dangers are mentioned at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: How many matters are given as help for the first danger?
questions.answer: Two matters.

questions.question: Do the two witnesses have to be famous people for their proof to count?
questions.answer: No. Even ordinary people can give valid witness.

questions.question: What can a person honestly say if he has not seen something?
questions.answer: He can say he does not see it.

questions.question: What does the passage say has already been proven strongly elsewhere?
questions.answer: This truth about faith.
